title: Then-and-now table
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Medieval peasants and the Black Death (Peasants, Princes & Pestilence)
source: Seeded from history/y5 lesson 19 (Then-and-now table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 19: The Black Death, 1348. To understand how the Black Death spread and how ideas about its causes then differ from what we know now

questions.q: When did the Black Death reach England?
questions.model: The timeline shows 1347 in the Mediterranean. The next year it reached England. So 1348.

questions.q: Name one thing people then thought caused it.
questions.a: Bad air, the planets or a punishment

questions.q: Complete a then-and-now table on causes, spread and protection, then answer: 'Why did people then not know the real cause?'
questions.a: Accurate table; answer: no microscopes, germs unknown
questions.model: Teacher fills in the 'causes' row first.

questions.q: Explain why fewer workers after the Black Death mattered for peasants.
questions.a: Workers were scarce, so they could ask for higher wages

questions.q: How was the Prophet's teaching about plague like quarantine today?
questions.a: Do not enter or leave a plague land: stay apart to stop the spread

questions.q: The Black Death reached England in:
Big question: without germ knowledge, what would you think?
questions.a: Many ideas, like bad air; we now know bacteria and fleas spread it
